accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England Year 1 word reading (read words containing taught GPCs and -s, -es, -ing, -ed, -er and -est endings; read other words of more than one syllable) and English Appendix 1 Year 2 (doubling after a single short vowel, dropping e before -ing, -ed, -er, -est), and Common Core RF.1.3f, RF.1.3g and RF.2.3d. The three -ed pronunciations (/ɪd/ after t and d, /t/ after voiceless sounds, /d/ after voiced sounds) and /ɪz/ for -es after sibilants match the Cambridge Grammar of the English Language; every lab word was checked for its beat count and root.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: splitting by syllable instead of by root (step 1 feedback 'jum is not the whole root', challenge col + dest and co + ldest, mastery m4), adding a beat to every -ed (step 1 prediction, drum step with jumped and played, challenge rested, mastery m3), reading hoping as hopping (step 3 pairs hopping/hoping and tapping/taped, practice p5, challenge hoped), and treating every final ing or er as an ending (step 4 king, sister, bed, bus; step 5 traps sister and king; challenge letter and ring).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagendread is a reading lab: the child taps the letter where the ending begins in a tile row, taps a drum once per beat and checks it against the -ed and -es beat rules, chooses the root of doubled and e-dropped words, sorts real endings from look-alike words by covering the end, and taps every inflected word in a wrapped sentence. None of these mechanics appears in flagvend (spelling verb endings) or flagsyl; lab_distinct stayed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule is met through the child's own action first: tapping f-a-s for faster returns 'fas is not the whole root. Keep going: the root is fast'; drumming two beats for jumped returns 'jump does not end in t or d, so ed just adds a t sound: jumpt. One beat'; choosing hop for hoping returns 'hoping has one letter before the ending. The root had an e that dropped off: hope'. Done screens list jump + ing, wanted ● ●, hopping ← hop, so the patterns are visible together.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions hold the tempting wrong answer the step disproves: that covering ing in jumping leaves jum (syllable split), that jumped has two beats, jump-ed (the drum step shows one), and that hopping and hoping share a root (step 3 separates hop and hope). The done line repeats the learner's prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages: plan as too short a root, planted as the whole word, rested with one beat, rested with three beats, skipe from a dropped-e misreading, skipp as the root, letter and ring as fake endings, two syllable-split errors for coldest, hop for hoped, and hoppe as a non-word. The lab steps add per-word messages for every wrong tap, drum count, root choice and sort.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short and concrete (Cover the ending with your finger. Read the root. Then add the ending: jump, jumping.) and pass the family readability limit in validate_lessons. Canvas letters are 30 px on white tiles; one instruction per round; the young class gives large buttons. The adult text uses the precise terms root, inflectional ending, GPC, syllable and the /ɪd/, /t/, /d/ allomorphs.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation stayed under 12% six-word overlap with every lesson, including Spelling Verb Endings, The Prefix un- and Word Parts as Clues. Every feedback line names the word, the root and the letters that matter.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (Android-size viewport, touch) in light and dark for all six steps after Show me: seven letter tiles fit in one row, the drum with Again and Check buttons fits with the beat dots above it, the root cards sit side by side, the two sorting boxes hold four words each, and sentence chips wrap onto two centred rows. The header was shortened after the first screenshots squeezed it.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed every task with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every tap has a labelled button ('Ending starts at letter 5: jump and ing', 'Tap the drum for one beat', 'hopping comes from hop', 'king: Just ends that way', 'dogs has an ending'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every feedback line. The drum word was moved to the theme text colour after the first dark screenshot showed low contrast.
